title: Nomura, Daiwa CEOs flag risk AI may spoil stock market rally
key_facts: Nomura Holdings CEO Kentaro Okuda and Daiwa Securities Group CEO Akihiko Ogino made the remarks on a panel at a Nikkei event in Tokyo on Thursday 8 Oct 2026.
Both expect Japan's stock rally to extend well into 2027, even as a possible reversal in AI investment is the main threat.
Ogino expects the Nikkei 225 to reach 80,000 this year and 88,000 toward the end of 2027; Okuda puts about 75,000 by year-end and above 80,000 by end-2027.
The Nikkei closed at 69,042.11 on Thursday.
Ogino expects the yen at about 160 per dollar through 2027; Okuda expects about 156 at year-end.
Both said public opposition to AI and data centres in countries including the US could lead to lower investment in the sector.
Both securities firms posted record profits last fiscal year.
quote_evidence: If sentiment toward AI were to shift and that trend went into reverse, I think that could pose a significant risk.
They can change their views dramatically over a very short period of time, causing sharp swings in asset prices.
why_it_matters_hint: Japan's stock rally depends on AI investment; two securities chiefs see a reversal as the main risk.
notes: Read in full from the Japan Times. Forecasts and remarks are the executives' own views at a public event, reported as such.
